_comment: DRAFT (dialogue-drafts lane 2026-07-06, NOT wired). 'The Price of a Favor' — the charmed villager: the verbatim-echo tell + the freed confession. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-riverfarm-design.md §2/§4 ('their pool line REPEATS the witch's line verbatim, the tell'). Voice contract: character-profiles-staging.md 'The charmed villager' (echoes the witch's current pool line verbatim, wrong register). Speaker 'Tam' = ORIGINAL+flag. THE ECHO IS STATIC IN THIS DRAFT — echo node texts are pinned copies of the witch's pool lines from pools/talk_pools.json; the spec's ideal is a DYNAMIC mirror of her current pool line (small sim seam, flagged OPEN in charmed_villager.md).

meet.speaker: Tam
meet.text: Tea first. Then troubles. The kettle has heard worse than yours.

text_variants.text: ...I keep starting sentences and finding they're MINE. You'd think that would feel ordinary by now. It doesn't. Not yet.

options.text: You're standing in a turnip row. There's no kettle, Tam.
Welcome back to your own tongue.

echo_two.speaker: Tam
echo_two.text: Prices are only cruel to people who wanted the thing for free.

tell.speaker: Tam
tell.text: The bent trees? They asked to grow that way. Everything here pays or is paid.
tell._comment: The [Observe] beat: the option's own result text should render as an observe-style toast at wiring time; the node text is Tam echoing ANOTHER witch line while you look — the wrongness compounds. Suggested observe toast (entity `observe` field, not dialogue): 'A red thread at the wrist, wound three times, ends tucked in. Farmhand hands, potter's-wheel stillness. The mouth is serving someone else's tea.'

echo_hold.speaker: Tam
echo_hold.text: Tea first. Then troubles. The kettle has heard worse than yours.

options.text: (There's no getting past the thread. The debt first.)

freed.speaker: Tam
freed.text: It was me. The favor. Mother's lungs went to water last winter, and the herb-woman's herbs weren't reaching. The witch named a fair price and I SAID yes — saying is easy in winter. ...Mother saw spring. I'd buy it twice over. I just thought the price would feel smaller by paying-time.

options.text: Prices feel like that. Pay it anyway.
You let the whole village's barley carry your bill.

resolve.speaker: Tam
resolve.text: Aye. I started this morning — wood split and stacked at the hollow before the fog burned off. A year of mornings. Cheap, held against spring. Don't tell Mother the arithmetic; she'd try to pay half.

options.text: Your secret's safe. Mind the mornings.

resolve_hard.speaker: Tam
resolve_hard.text: ...I know. I watched it grey from my own window and told myself it was weather. You want me ashamed — I got there first, weeks ago, with the door locked. What's left is the paying. I started this morning. Wood split, stacked, at the hollow. A year of mornings, and every one of them owed.

options.text: Then we're done here. Pay it well.

mornings.speaker: Tam
mornings.text: Up before the birds, back before the dew's off. Split, stack, sweep, kettle. She doesn't thank me — that'd muddy the ledger, she says. But there's bread warming on the sill when I finish, most days. Warm bread's not thanks. It's just... adjacent.
